name: Bollinger-z and RSI double-oversold reversion (1h)
rationale: Requiring BOTH a negative band z-score and a low RSI on 1h demands two orthogonal reads of oversold — statistical distance from the mean AND momentum exhaustion — to agree before fading, which strips out the false positives each shows alone. The other side is the capitulating holder selling near a local bottom. Edge persists because genuine dual-confirmed exhaustion is rarer and revert-prone. Distinct from the single-signal reversion specs: it is the confluence, not either leg. Disconfirmer: exits when RSI recovers past its exit level, or the stop fires if both signals were the opening of a real breakdown.
catalyst: confluence of statistical and momentum oversold
